key_insight: The paper shows that the choice of regression objective for tabular deep learning is an important but underexplored design decision, and that claims about better-than-MSE losses must be judged under consistent evaluation. It also argues that global early stopping has practical limits, so training protocol details can strongly affect conclusions.
problem_solved: This work addresses the lack of a fair, apples-to-apples comparison between regression objectives for deep tabular models. Previous studies used different datasets, backbones, and evaluation setups, making it hard to know which loss functions actually help in practice.
method: Systematically re-evaluates multiple regression objectives against standard MSE for tabular deep regression.
Controls for differences in datasets, model backbones, and evaluation protocols to make comparisons more reliable.
Examines the role and limitations of global early stopping in determining reported performance.
impact: For practitioners, this paper helps clarify when alternative regression losses are worth trying and when reported gains may be artifacts of training/evaluation choices. It provides a more trustworthy basis for selecting objectives in tabular deep learning pipelines.
visual_elements: Side-by-side bar chart comparing regression objectives across datasets
Pipeline diagram showing dataset, backbone, objective, and evaluation protocol controls
Early stopping timeline illustrating why global early stopping can mislead results
Icon-based summary of common objectives vs. MSE
paper_title: Revisiting Tabular Deep Regression: Objectives and the Limits of Global Early Stopping
paper_authors: Danil Rudenko, Georgii Bulgakov, Nikolay Kartashev, Ivan Rubachev, Daniil Krasylnikov
